why: Minimum swaps to sort a 1/2/3 array has a closed form from the 3x3 table m[a][b] = how many b's sit in the zone where a's belong: fix 2-cycles first (min(m[a][b], m[b][a])), the rest form 3-cycles costing 2 swaps each. Updates move the zone boundaries, so each zone count is a range-count query: three Fenwick/segment trees, one per value.
hints: After sorting, the first c1 cells hold 1s, the next c2 hold 2s, the rest 3s. Count how many of each value sit in each zone.

A 1 in the 2-zone and a 2 in the 1-zone fix each other with one swap; pair those up for all three value pairs. Whatever is still misplaced forms 3-cycles, and each cycle of 3 needs 2 swaps: answer = pairs + 2 * (remaining / 3).
Keep one Fenwick tree per value for range counts. Each query: point update, recompute c1, c2, then 6 range counts. O(log n) per query.
pitfalls: The zone boundaries change with every update (counts change), so you cannot precompute zones once.
An update that writes the same value must still produce an answer.
Recounting the array per query is O(n * q) = 10^10: too slow.
